claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Pre-firing marks occur at most Indus sites in the second half of the fourth millennium BCE.
claims.assessment: Recovered Mehrgarh and Harappa records support early marks at those sites; Rehman Dheri has a stratified incised series. The proportion of all Indus sites is not established.
claims.missing: A dated site census and common pre/post-firing classification.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Mehrgarh marks identify potter or owner during a shared firing.
claims.assessment: Quivron proposes production/workshop identification; Coningham discusses communal ownership/risk using Quivron 1997. Function has a published precedent but is not independently authenticated.
source_locations: Quivron 1980 pp. 275, 278; Coningham 2002 pp. 93–94 citing Quivron 1997 pp. 53, 55, 61
claims.missing: Primary 1997 chapter and joined batch/vessel/mark registers.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Marks nearly disappear when a new kiln type appears.
claims.assessment: Quivron 1980 notes a decline by around 2400 BCE; Coningham reports a peak near 2700 and later decline. Miller documents contemporary open-air/updraft methods, including Nausharo II. A causal replacement comparison was not recovered.
source_locations: Quivron p. 278; Coningham p. 93; Miller pp. 42–43, 47–49, 57
claims.missing: Mark-frequency denominators by dated firing technology, sampling and ware controls.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: The same early mark repertoire appears on seals in the late fourth to early third millennium BCE.
claims.assessment: Quivron 1980 p. 275 explicitly describes contemporary seals as having a different, restricted repertoire. Durrani/Kenoyer propose selected similarities. The full shared repertoire needs a sign-level test.
source_locations: Quivron pp. 275, 279; Durrani p. 28; Kenoyer pp. 220–226
claims.missing: Fixed feature mapping, rare compounds, independent chronology and complete mark/seal comparison population.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Caption name Rakandere, an ivory button seal from northwestern Baluchistan.
claims.assessment: Rehman Dheri is supported by Frenez 2018 p. 171 n. 5 and Kenoyer/Meadow 2010 p. liv, naming CISI 2 Rhd-1. Button seal is their terminology for the rectangular two-hole object; the caption geography is wrong. The primary phase alternatives are IA/IB, not Period II.
source_locations: 1988 pp. 17–18, 25, 28; 1995 catalogue 54 p. 201, photo p. 206; Introduction p.vii; Kenoyer Table 2 p. 221
claims.missing: Independent lecture-image match; original field registration and a resolution of layer 6/level 19 versus layer 12 and PeriodIB.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Harappa has shared signs on seals/pottery before 2800 BCE and a sealing from a fireplace radiocarbon-dated near 2800.
claims.assessment: Ravi pottery marks and a carved bone fragment predate the Kot Diji phase. Published intaglio seals and clay sealings begin in 2800–2600 BCE. Gallery confirms hearth find/circa 2800 label; direct radiocarbon join is missing.
source_locations: 1999 Figure 4 item 6; 2006 Figure 5:9; 2010 p.li/Table 1; 2005 p. 209/Table 2; gallery 136–137
claims.missing: Sample number, lab determination, calibration and deposit/specimen join establishing a before 2800 endpoint.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: Frenez says writing was reintroduced by Buddhist merchants in the fifth century after priestly preference for oral transmission; BCE is inferred from context.
claims.assessment: Compare with unselected Allchin/Coningham 450–350 BCE, Volume II Porunthal 580–520 and 560–410 BCE, and the A/high Ashokan endpoint. No merchant carriers identified by those dates.
source_locations: parent dating assessments for anuradhapura, porunthal-I, kodumanal, keeladi, ashoka-brahmi
claims.missing: Evidence joining the earliest inscriptions to particular transmitters, routes and institutions.

claims.statement_attributed_to: Dennys Frenez through coordinator caption check
claims.statement: A forthcoming group paper concerns Indus-style cuneiform and Linear Elamite seals. He also says some legends encode Sumerian names and others names neither Sumerian nor Akkadian.
claims.assessment: Published examples are identified separately in contact-items.json. 2024 CV lists the related paper in preparation; live title searches found no final published paper. The talk’s claim is retained as forthcoming.
source_locations: CV PDF 7; 2018 Figure 10; 2023 Figure 3; Laursen no. 28; 2026 primary abstract
claims.missing: Final publication and complete object catalogue; authenticated paired Indus/foreign-script inscription.
